facts.text: Founded as Centreville in 1815 at key crossroads, Carrollton was renamed in 1834 after Charles Carroll of Carrollton, the last surviving signer of the Declaration of Independence.
The 1885 Carroll County Courthouse anchors the historic town square, showcasing preserved 19th‑century architecture that still defines Carrollton’s skyline.
The Daniel McCook House, listed on the National Register since 1976, stands as a reminder of the Fighting McCooks’ Civil War legacy in Carrollton.
A branch of the Wheeling and Lake Erie Railway cuts through Carrollton, terminating at the Carroll County Industrial Park and linking the village to regional trade.
Carrollton’s streets weave through State Routes 39 and 43, while Routes 9 and 332 also pass, making it a modest crossroads hub.
The village prides itself on a strong sense of community, rich history, and a commitment to progress, according to its official website.
